flags.message: MCP CourtListener search failed with a rate limit error (HTTP 429). Degraded gracefully to Google Web Search for case context.

The frozen context records 6 amicus briefs, but the provisioned snapshot contains 13 amicus filing entries: 6 use 'Brief amicus curiae' and 7 use 'Brief amici curiae.' This appears to be a singular/plural parsing gap. The prediction uses the harness-owned frozen count of 6 for the amicus-increment claim.

The frozen context records amicus_briefs=6, but the same 2026-08-16 snapshot contains 13 proceedings entries expressly recording amicus filings. The amicus-increment probability is stated against the harness-owned frozen count of 6; the mismatch should be reviewed before interpreting that claim.

The frozen context records amicus_briefs=6, but the provisioned snapshot contains 13 distinct docket entries beginning 'Brief amicus curiae' or 'Brief amici curiae.' The count appears to recognize singular 'amicus' entries while missing plural 'amici' entries, compromising the amicus-increment conditioning state.

The amicus counter (_AMICUS_RE in pipeline/interim_signals.py) matches 'amicus curiae' only, so the seven 'Brief amici curiae ...' entries on this docket are not counted: the frozen amicus_briefs=6 sits against 13 amicus filings a human would count. The counter's docstring registers one-entry-many-filers as a deliberate undercount, but the singular/plural miss looks unintentional and materially understates the stakes signal on multi-filer dockets like this one. My amicus-increment claim is stated against the counter's own semantics, so the cell is consistent either way.

Frozen context reports amicus_briefs: 6, but the 2026-08-16 snapshot shows 13 amicus docket entries. The 6 entries captioned 'Brief amicus curiae' (singular) match the frozen count exactly, so the counter appears to miss 'Brief amici curiae' (plural) entries. The amicus-increment claim was stated against the frozen 6 assuming the same counter runs at resolution; if the counting changes, the claim's resolution shifts mechanically.

CourtListener MCP was unavailable for this cell (HTTP 429, daily rate limit exceeded on the first call). The prediction rests on the provisioned snapshot, the committed statpack, one corpus query, and general legal context; no live docket or filed-document text was retrieved.

Frozen context reports amicus_briefs: 6, but the same-day snapshot shows 13 amicus filings on the docket. The 6 matches exactly the entries reading 'Brief amicus curiae' (singular); the seven 'Brief amici curiae' (plural) entries appear uncounted, so the amicus escalation signal systematically undercounts group briefs. My amicus-increment probability assumes the resolver counts the same way as the freezer; if resolution counts all amicus entries the claim resolves true immediately.
CourtListener MCP search tool failed due to rate limit HTTP 429.

The provisioned brief-in-opposition.txt concatenates the January cert opposition with the July respondent merits brief and is marked truncated; extraction stops after merits-brief page 37 before the full final-agency-action argument. No petitioner merits-brief text was provisioned. The prediction used the available respondent introduction, summary, partial argument, and earlier cert opposition, and records the resulting limitation in reasoning.md.

This event is the grant-moment merits forecast opened on 2026-03-09, but the provisioned 2026-08-16 snapshot contains later merits filings and the file named brief-in-opposition.txt concatenates the respondent's 2026-07-20 merits brief after the cert-stage opposition. A whole-file heading search inadvertently surfaced scattered later-brief headings and snippets; I disregarded them. The forecast uses the grant-moment petition, cert-stage opposition, questions presented, general precedent, and prior-Term base rate.

CourtListener MCP was rate-limited (HTTP 429, shared 1400/day quota exhausted, ~89 min to reset) on this cell's first and only attempted call (~18:00Z). The cell degraded gracefully per the prompt: predicted from the provisioned documents, the docket snapshot, the committed statpack, and corpus tooling. Cells later in a large fan-out day may routinely hit this quota.

documents.json lists one kind='brief-in-opposition' entry whose url field carries two pipe-joined URLs (the Jan 16 2026 BIO and the Jul 20 2026 merits brief of respondent) under entry_date 'Jul 20 2026', and the provisioned text file concatenates both filings. The content was usable — indeed valuable for a briefed-moment merits cell — but the kind/provenance labeling is misleading; petitioners' merits brief (May 22 2026) has no counterpart entry.

The grant order says this companion was granted only as to the question presented in lead docket No. 25-238, but the provisioned documents contain only No. 25-566's petition and opposition. The exact granted lead question was therefore absent. One permitted CourtListener MCP search for the lead docket returned HTTP 429 and no data, so the forecast uses only the shared assault-weapons issue established by the provisioned record.

This docket (25-566) was consolidated into Viramontes v. Cook County, No. 25-238, at the 2026-06-30 grant, and the docket's own final entry says all future filings and activity will be reflected on 25-238's docket. The merits judgment may therefore never appear as an entry here — outcome resolution for this event will likely need to read the lead docket.
CourtListener MCP search was rate-limited (HTTP 429). Degraded gracefully by using Google Web Search to ascertain the merits arguments.
CourtListener MCP tool 'search' returned HTTP 429 Rate limit exceeded. Degraded gracefully to provisioned inputs and corpus tooling, but could not retrieve merits briefs or lower court opinion.

This grant-moment cell was provisioned with an August 2026 snapshot containing post-grant merits filings, and brief-in-opposition.txt appends Intel's July 2026 merits response after the December 2025 cert BIO (documents.json also marks the combined file truncated). I excluded the appended merits brief and all other post-grant advocacy, using only the pre-grant record for the forecast.

The provisioned 'brief-in-opposition' document bundles two distinct filings — the Dec 9, 2025 brief in opposition and Intel's Jul 2, 2026 merits response brief — under one document kind, with both source URLs concatenated in documents.json's url field (pipe-separated) and truncated: true across the bundle. The extra merits-brief text was valuable for this briefed-moment cell, but the kind label understates what the file holds, and the petitioners' Apr 23, 2026 merits brief has no counterpart document; a merits-stage document kind would make the provisioning symmetric.

The provisioned document of kind 'brief-in-opposition' (98pp, truncated) concatenates two distinct filings — the Dec 9 2025 cert-stage BIO and the Jul 2 2026 merits response brief (its url field carries both PDFs pipe-separated). Helpful for a merits cell, but the kind label understates the content and a cert-stage consumer of this kind could unknowingly read merits-stage text.

CourtListener MCP was unusable for this cell: the first search call returned HTTP 429 (shared 1400/day limit exhausted, ~100-minute retry window), so the cell degraded to provisioned inputs, the committed statpack, and web search per the retrieval contract. Late cells in a large fan-out will predictably hit this; a per-cell call budget or a workflow-level backoff would keep them from running without live CourtListener access.

record/documents/documents.json labels a single 72-page file as a brief in opposition but gives a pipe-separated source combining the February 2026 cert BIO and the August 2026 corrected respondent merits brief; the local text concatenates both documents. I isolated and used the merits portion, but the manifest's kind, date, and source do not describe one document.

gaps.label: No brief in opposition was available at the arrival moment.

A cases-citing-authority search (rather than own-cite matching) would make the corpus useful for doctrine-line priors; the citation filter returned nothing for Bruen/Heller at a cost of 1329 ranged GETs / ~348 MB

A cases-citing-this-authority search (citation graph) would have answered 'how have this Court's recent channeling cases come out' from the corpus; the --citation filter is own-cites-only and sparse, so it returned nothing for Johnson v. Robison.
A citation-filter corpus query that matches nothing still costs ~348 MB of ranged reads (1329 GETs); a cheap existence probe or a coverage warning before the transfer would save most of that.
A citation-filtered fedcourts query cost ~348 MB of ranged reads to return zero rows; a cheap existence check on the sparse citation column before the scan would save that egress.
A citing-cases graph (cases citing a given authority) — the --citation filter is a known-case lookup, so precedent-similarity retrieval by cited authority is not possible
A consolidated-docket pointer in the record would help: this docket froze at the grant and all future activity lands on the lead case No. 25-238, which the snapshot only reveals in free text

A corpus filter for petitioner representation status (pro se vs counseled) within the paid segment would sharpen exactly this cell's largest adjustment, which currently rests on general knowledge rather than a published cut.
A first-class fetch-and-extract tool for current Supreme Court merits filings would avoid ad hoc PDF extraction.
A grant-moment snapshot frozen on the event's opening date would prevent later merits filings from entering this cell.
